newsitem.title: UK: U.S. T-bonds steady in London, swap trades dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bonds steady in London, swap trades dominate.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady in London on Wednesday, with swap activity in the three to five year sector dominating otherwise quiet trade, dealers said.
They added the market may drift lower into Friday's inflation and sales data, the only focal point for trade.
"Since we didn't sustain the gains made two days ago yesterday, people may try to test the downside again," said one dealer at a U.S. bank here.
"I'm looking for the future to continue range trading between about 106-30 and 107-24."
By 0948 GMT, the June T-note future was steady at 107-13. The 30-year cash long bond was at 94-04 to yield 7.10 percent, up from 94-03 in Tokyo and unchanged from the New York close.
Phil Tyson, international economist at HSBC Markets here, was slightly negative on Treasuries near term.

"There's not much focus until we get to Friday with the PPI and retail sales data," he said. "But the bias is still fairly cautious and I'm looking for U.S. yields to trend higher over the next few weeks."
He added that over the next few days he was neutral to slightly negative.

Tyson said he expected the producer price data to help relieve some inflation concerns, but with retail sales seen fairly robust, he expected a slight steepening of the curve, mainly from the long end.
The trader said swap activity had dominated morning trade again on Wednesday.

"Most of the activity is swap related both ways in the front, threes and fives," he said. "I've heard some Japanese life companies selling fives and buying tens, but activity is pretty light overall."
